releases.title: Route maps on every card

highlights.title: See the route
highlights.text: Runs, rides and walks show their route map right on the card, between the stats and the photos.

highlights.title: Drawn when Strava sends no picture
highlights.text: When Strava only sends the route line, the digest draws it, with start and finish marked.

highlights.title: Tap for details
highlights.text: Tap the map to open the activity's details, where the same map appears.

changes: Route map on each activity card (Comfortable, and Compact or Tiny once expanded); indoor activities show none
The route is drawn from Strava's encoded route line when there is no map picture, or when the picture fails to load
The details sheet shows the card's map instead of a separate picture
fixes: The details sheet sometimes showed one of the activity's photos as its "route map"; the page preview picture is now used only when it really is a map

releases.title: Opens every time, and shows what AI adds

highlights.title: Opens every time
highlights.text: No more blank screen when opening from the widget, after quick taps or with slow iCloud.

highlights.title: See what AI adds
highlights.text: Without a key, a short card now and then shows what AI adds to your comments.

highlights.title: Start-up log
highlights.text: Settings › Updates › Start-up log shows what happened the last times it opened.

changes: The digest opens on an empty dark window first, then the launch screen, then reads its data, so a page is always drawn
Quick taps on the widget open one window, not several
Your Strava feed starts loading just after the first screen is up; the update check follows a few seconds later
Without an AI key, an invitation card appears at most every 3 days (weekly after four "Later"s), never over another sheet or an update offer; "Don't remind me again" stops it for good
Turn on AI opens AI settings with Add key highlighted; removing your last key brings the invitation back from the next launch
Settings › Updates has a Start-up log row with the last 40 lines
If a saved file turns out to be damaged, the digest keeps a copy of it, starts that file fresh and tells you so
fixes: Opening the digest could stay on a blank screen, most often from the widget or with slow iCloud
A comment history or settings file that iCloud hadn't delivered could be saved over with an empty one
If opening stalls, the screen now says so and shows the start-up log instead of staying blank
A damaged comment history or settings file no longer stops the digest from saving your changes
Turn on AI now highlights Add key for the provider in use, not always Claude's

releases.title: Learns from more of your comments

highlights.title: Finds your comments
highlights.text: Learn my style now recognises far more of your own comments among everything it reads.

highlights.title: Knows your name
highlights.text: Looks up your name on Strava, and spots it shortened (Gediminas S.) or without Lithuanian accents.

highlights.title: Shows what it read
highlights.text: Settings says how many comments it read and how many were yours. Only yours shape your style.

changes: Settings › Learn my style shows how many comments were read on how many activities, next to how many were yours
When it finds too few, the message says how many it read and whose name it looked for
fixes: A comment's author was sometimes taken from the comment's own ID, so most of your comments weren't recognised as yours
Your name was only known when your own activities were in the loaded feed; it's now read from your Strava profile
Shortened names ("Gediminas S.") and names written with or without Lithuanian letters now match

releases.title: A simpler comment composer

highlights.title: Less to choose from
highlights.text: The composer is just your comment, the moods and the AI ideas.

highlights.title: My style leads
highlights.text: ✨ My style is the first mood and the default, with your instructions behind every idea.

highlights.title: Tidier settings
highlights.text: The Custom prompt box is gone; your instructions in Comment writing cover it.

changes: Removed the ✎ Custom mood, its prompt field in the composer and the Custom prompt setting
Removed the Improve my draft row (Punchier, Funnier, Shorter, Warmer, In my style, Rephrase)
A saved Custom mood now opens as ✨ My style

releases.title: Comments that sound like you

highlights.title: A proper comment composer
highlights.text: 💬 opens a pop-up with your draft, AI ideas and one-tap rewrites: punchier, funnier, shorter, warmer.

highlights.title: Your instructions, every time
highlights.text: Write the rules once in Settings, like a witty British running mate, and every AI comment follows them.

highlights.title: Learns your style
highlights.text: Reads up to 50 of your own comments and writes like you when you tap ✨ My style.

changes: Tapping 💬 opens a comment composer pop-up instead of a box inside the card; drafts are kept if you close it
Improve my draft: Punchier, Funnier, Shorter, Warmer, In my style and Rephrase rewrite what you have written, three options each
✨ My style mood, first in the list: your instructions plus the style learned from your comments

Settings › Comment writing: instructions for every AI comment (a British running-mate default, Reset to default), how many comments to learn from (5 to 50, default 20), Learn my style with progress, the learned profile and Clear
Your instructions now take priority over the app's own defaults in every AI request; the safety rules still always apply
Comments you post through the digest are remembered on the iPhone (last 50) as the surest examples of your style
AI settings › usage lists style learning separately

releases.title: Your activities, on top

highlights.title: Your activities first
highlights.text: Your latest one to three activities sit above everyone else's, with the kudos and comments you received.

highlights.title: See who cheered
highlights.text: Tap one to see who gave kudos and read every comment, without opening the Strava app.

highlights.title: Like comments
highlights.text: Tap the heart on a comment to like it right in the digest.

changes: "Your activities" strip at the top of the digest: your activities from today and yesterday, newest first, up to three side by side, each with kudos and comments received
The strip is hidden when you have no activities of your own, and works whether or not "Show my own activities" is on
Tapping one opens a sheet with who gave kudos (with a full list) and all comments
Like or unlike a comment with its heart; the first like goes through Strava's own button and teaches the app the request, later likes are sent directly
If Strava offers no way to like comments, the hearts turn read-only and say so
Today's view reads back to yesterday in the background so yesterday's activities appear in the strip

releases.title: Kudos at a glance

highlights.title: A new widget look
highlights.text: The kudos widget now wears the Daily Digest logo on its dark tile, like the other apps.

highlights.title: Every size
highlights.text: Small, medium and large on the Home Screen, plus inline, round and rectangular on the Lock Screen.

highlights.title: Never an error
highlights.text: Works offline from the last summary and says when it's out of date, never Scriptable's error text.

changes: Home Screen widget in the shared frame (widgets blueprint 1.0.0): logo tile and name, people waiting for kudos as the big number, who is waiting with their sport, early-riser badge and ×n, and "of 15 today, 10:22" at the bottom
Large widget adds the day's PRs and early risers; Lock Screen widgets show "👍 15 waiting for kudos"
The widget reads a summary saved on this iPhone, so it works offline; after the time set in Settings › Widget › "Mark the widget as out of date after" (12 h by default) its bottom line turns amber
Before the digest has loaded today the widget says "Open to load today"; a failing widget shows the app name and "Tap to open" instead of an error
Settings › Built with now lists the widgets blueprint

releases.title: Catch up. Cheer. Move on.

highlights.title: A logo of its own
highlights.text: The route digest: a route from a teal start to a rose finish, with two digest lines.

highlights.title: Launch screen
highlights.text: The route draws itself and the tagline appears for about 2 seconds; tap to skip.

highlights.title: Branded everywhere
highlights.text: The logo sits in the header, on a day nobody has posted yet and in the README.

changes: New Daily Digest logo (route digest): docs/logo.svg and a 1024 px app icon, docs/icon-1024.png
Launch screen shown for 2.4 s with a short animation and the tagline "Catch up. Cheer. Move on."; tap to skip; still with Reduce Motion (shared launch-screen blueprint 1.0.0)
Logo mark in the sticky header with "Digest" in the brand rose, the logo on an empty day, and at the top of the README
Settings › Built with now lists the launch-screen blueprint

releases.title: Pace at a glance

highlights.title: Pace on every line
highlights.text: Runs, walks and hikes show their pace next to the distance in Compact and Tiny.

highlights.title: Roomier Tiny lines
highlights.text: A compact 👍 button leaves space for all the indicators; none is ever cut in half.

highlights.title: See who you've cheered
highlights.text: In Tiny, the 👍 turns into ✓ once you've given kudos, so you never tap twice.

changes: Pace indicator after distance in the Compact and Tiny layouts
Tiny layout: compact round 👍 kudos button (✓ once given)
Tiny layout: indicators that don't fit are hidden whole instead of being cut off

releases.title: Peek, then dive in

highlights.title: Tap to expand
highlights.text: In Compact, each activity is one tidy line; tap it to open the full card in place.

highlights.title: See what's inside
highlights.text: Distance, trophies and photo counts on every line, so you know what's worth opening.

highlights.title: Tiny opens in place
highlights.text: Tap an athlete in Tiny to expand their activities right there, no sheet.

changes: Compact layout folds each activity to its title, time and indicators; tap to expand or collapse
Indicators for distance (or time), achievements and photos, with PRs highlighted in gold
Tiny layout shows the same indicators and expands an athlete's activities in place
Expanded cards stay open while details load in the background
The details sheet always shows the full card

releases.title: Make it yours

highlights.title: Colours and layout
highlights.text: Six colour palettes or Auto, plus Comfortable, Compact or a one-line Tiny layout.

highlights.title: Text size and font
highlights.text: Pick Small to Larger text and a sans or serif font for names and titles.

highlights.title: Tune everything
highlights.text: Feed depth, time limits, widget refresh and more, each with Reset.

changes: New Settings sheet (sliders icon): Appearance, Digest, AI comments, Updates, tunables and Built with; changes apply at once, no Save button
Appearance shared with the other apps: Auto plus six palettes (Strava orange in all), Comfortable, Compact or Tiny layout, four text sizes, sans or serif headline font
Tiny layout: one line per athlete with their main stat and kudos; tap a name for the full activity
Tunables with ranges and Reset: feed pages, extra pages per day, details opened at once, time limits, days in the header, comment ideas per tap, widget refresh, athlete ID
Settings move from the Keychain to settings.json in iCloud Drive › Scriptable › StravaFeed; your choices move over automatically
Built with: the blueprints this app follows, with links to read them
Updates identify the app by its APP_ID line, as the in-app updates blueprint describes

releases.title: Claude or OpenAI, plus a settings fix

highlights.title: Claude or OpenAI
highlights.text: ✨ Comment ideas now work with either provider. Switch any time in AI settings.

highlights.title: Pick any model
highlights.text: Load the models your own key can use, choose one and test the connection.

highlights.title: See your token usage
highlights.text: Tokens per day, feature and model, so you always know what AI costs you.

changes: Brings back everything from 1.9.0 (AI settings, Claude or OpenAI, model picker, token usage), which the 1.8.2 release accidentally undid

releases.title: Claude or OpenAI, your choice

highlights.title: Claude or OpenAI
highlights.text: ✨ Comment ideas now work with either provider. Switch any time in AI settings.

highlights.title: Pick any model
highlights.text: Load the models your own key can use, choose one and test the connection.

highlights.title: See your token usage
highlights.text: Tokens per day, feature and model, so you always know what AI costs you.

changes: New AI settings sheet (⚙︎ › AI settings): Claude and OpenAI keys, model picker loaded from your key, connection test, token usage per day, feature and model
Keys are entered in a native secure prompt and stored in the iOS Keychain; the page only ever sees them masked
Comment ideas go through one shared AI call, following the app-blueprints AI configuration
✨ Suggest, moods and language buttons stay hidden until a key is saved
Comment ideas are labelled with the provider that wrote them
Your existing OpenAI key and model move over automatically
The thinking-effort setting is gone: choose a model instead

releases.title: Clearer settings errors

highlights.title: Errors you can see
highlights.text: If a setting can't be saved, the settings sheet now scrolls to the message.

fixes: A settings error could appear below the visible area, so a failed save looked like nothing happened

releases.title: Tidier header

highlights.title: Matching header icons
highlights.text: Settings and refresh are now the same size and easier to tap.

changes: Settings and refresh icons drawn as matching line icons with larger tap areas
fixes: Settings icon looked smaller than the refresh icon

releases.title: Settings, right in the app

highlights.title: Settings screen
highlights.text: Tap the gear in the header to change how the digest works, no code editing.

highlights.title: Manage your API key
highlights.text: Replace or remove your OpenAI key any time; only its last 4 characters are shown.

highlights.title: Check for updates now
highlights.text: See your version and look for a new one with a single tap.

changes: Settings sheet behind a gear icon in the header
AI settings: API key, default mood, custom prompt, language, model and thinking effort
Digest settings: own activities, extra details, names on the widget
Update settings: turn offers on or off, check now
Advanced: Strava athlete ID
Settings are kept in the iOS Keychain, so updates never reset them

releases.title: Comments in your mood

highlights.title: Comment moods
highlights.text: Pick Funny, Energetic, Serious or Funky and get three comments in that tone.

highlights.title: Your own prompt
highlights.text: Type how you want it, like "tease about the rain", and the AI follows.

highlights.title: Remembers your style
highlights.text: Your mood and custom prompt stay selected for next time.

changes: Mood chips in the comment box: Funny, Energetic, Serious, Funky and Custom
Custom prompt field that drives the AI suggestions
Mood and custom prompt are remembered between runs

releases.title: Never miss an update

highlights.title: Update reminders
highlights.text: The digest tells you when a new version is out. Tap Later and it waits two days before asking again.

highlights.title: One-tap update
highlights.text: Update right from the digest. No need to run the installer again.

highlights.title: See what's new first
highlights.text: Every update shows its three best features before you install it.

changes: Update check on start, with a pitch sheet showing the top three highlights
Later snoozes update reminders for two days
Version number shown at the bottom of the digest
Release notes now live in releases.json, with a generated CHANGELOG.md

releases.title: Kudos to everyone, with style

highlights.title: Pinned header
highlights.text: Today, Yesterday and the 👍 All button stay at the top wherever you scroll.

highlights.title: Kudos celebration
highlights.text: Thumbs fly from the centre to every athlete's photo, with a ✓ as each one lands.

highlights.title: Cleaner screen
highlights.text: No more stuck pop-up at the bottom, and kudos counts look right again.

changes: Sticky header in the Go2FGym style with a compact day switcher and an always-visible 👍 All button
Celebration animation when giving kudos to everyone
Day switcher limited to Today and Yesterday
fixes: Pop-up message no longer peeks out at the bottom of the screen
Kudos counts were drawn as large orange circles

releases.title: A proper photo viewer

highlights.title: Zoom photos
highlights.text: Double-tap or pinch to zoom, and drag around while zoomed in.

highlights.title: Thumbnail strip
highlights.text: See the previous and next photos, and tap one to jump straight to it.

highlights.title: Big close button
highlights.text: An always-visible Close photo button, so you never leave the app by accident.

changes: Pinch and double-tap zoom in the photo viewer
Thumbnail strip with the current photo highlighted
Large Close photo button at the bottom
Date bar stays pinned while scrolling
fixes: Swiping between photos stopped working after zoom was added

releases.title: Stable comments

highlights.title: No more crashes
highlights.text: Posting a comment no longer loads Strava's heavy page every time.

highlights.title: Faster comments
highlights.text: After the first comment, the rest are sent with one small request.

highlights.title: Honest confirmation
highlights.text: Only Strava's real reply to your comment counts as posted.

changes: Learns Strava's comment request once and reuses it
fixes: Scriptable could be closed by iOS while posting a comment
A tracking request could be mistaken for a posted comment

releases.title: Widget and details

highlights.title: Kudos widget
highlights.text: See how many people are waiting for your kudos on the Home or Lock Screen.

highlights.title: Activity details
highlights.text: Route map, all stats and bigger photos, without leaving the digest.

highlights.title: Pull to refresh
highlights.text: Drag the digest down at the top to reload today's feed.

changes: Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets
Activity details sheet with route map
Pull to refresh
Loading screen with a running figure and a live post counter

releases.title: Who's waiting for kudos

highlights.title: Waiting first
highlights.text: People still waiting for your kudos are grouped at the top.

highlights.title: Comment animation
highlights.text: Watch your comment fly to your friend, with confetti when it lands.

highlights.title: Fun loading screen
highlights.text: A runner collects posts while a counter ticks up.

changes: Waiting for your kudos and Kudos given sections
Screen locks with an animation while a comment is sent
Animated loading screen with post counter

releases.title: First public release

highlights.title: Kudos to everyone
highlights.text: Two taps give one kudos to each person in the day's feed.

highlights.title: AI comment ideas
highlights.text: Funny, friendly comments built from each activity's real stats.

highlights.title: Grouped by athlete
highlights.text: One card per person with the numbers that matter up front.

changes: Daily digest of the people you follow, grouped by athlete
One kudos per person, plus kudos to everyone
AI comment suggestions in English and Lithuanian
Early-riser badges, photo viewer, start times and PRs
